name: Paris Grey
editorial_article:
Paris Grey (born Shanna Jackson, November 5, 1965) is a highly influential American singer and songwriter, best recognized as the definitive vocal voice of the pioneering Detroit techno and house act, Inner City. Emerging from a background in gospel music, she brought a soulful, emotive depth to the burgeoning electronic scene of the late 1980s. Her collaboration with producer Kevin Saunderson turned Inner City into a global phenomenon, producing seminal tracks that bridged the gap between underground techno and pop radio success.

Beyond her iconic work with Inner City, including landmark anthems such as "Big Fun" and "Good Life," Grey maintained a prolific solo career and collaborated with various figures in the dance music underground, spanning from Chicago house legends like Fast Eddie to European dance producers. Her ability to infuse synthesized, mechanistic rhythm tracks with heartfelt, human melody became a blueprint for the "diva-led" vocal house sound. Throughout the 1990s and beyond, she remained an active figure in the dance community, continuing to record and tour while cementing her status as a fundamental architect of the electronic vocal tradition. Her contributions were not just limited to Inner City; her versatility allowed her to work with diverse producers across different facets of electronic music, ensuring that her influence resonated far beyond Detroit's borders. Her career remains a testament to the power of fusing traditional vocal performance with the cutting-edge, experimental sounds of the early rave era, leaving an indelible mark on dance music history.
